title: MFA re-registration after a phone change
text: When a user replaces or loses their phone, the authenticator app no longer produces valid codes. The service desk clears the registered methods in the identity portal and the user re-registers at next sign-in. Verify identity with a video call before clearing methods. Sign-in error HL-1043 means the second factor was rejected.

title: Account lockout after failed sign-ins
text: Ten failed password attempts within fifteen minutes lock the account for thirty minutes. Error HL-1050 is shown during the lockout. Do not unlock early unless the user's manager confirms the request in the ticket. Repeated lockouts from one address go to the SEC-TRIAGE queue.

title: Password reset self-service
text: Users reset a forgotten password on the self-service page after proving two registered methods. The new password must be at least fourteen characters. A password reset does not clear MFA registration.

title: Sign-in policy overview
text: Sign-in to internal applications requires a password and a second factor. Conditional access blocks sign-in from unmanaged devices outside the office network. This document describes policy, not troubleshooting.

title: Node DiskPressure and image pruning
text: Alert NW-DISK-17 fires when a Kubernetes node reports DiskPressure. The kubelet evicts pods until disk usage falls. Check growth under /var/lib/containerd from unpruned images and run the image prune job in a change window.

title: Expanding a VM data disk
text: To grow a VM data disk, snapshot it first, resize the disk in the portal, then extend the filesystem with growpart and resize2fs. Only an OS disk needs the VM deallocated before resizing.

title: Log rotation on application servers
text: Application logs in /var/log/app rotate daily and keep fourteen files. A full /var partition on an application server usually means rotation failed. Check the logrotate status file and its cron job, then compress or remove old logs.

title: Storage capacity planning
text: Capacity reviews run quarterly. Teams forecast disk growth from ninety days of usage and request storage through the capacity form. Nothing in this document is an incident procedure.

title: Restoring a database to a point in time
text: Point-in-time restore creates a new database from the backup chain and never overwrites the original. Choose a restore time within the seven-day window, restore to a new name, validate row counts, then swap connection strings.

title: Backup job failure BKP-E221
text: Error BKP-E221 means the nightly backup could not write to the vault because the storage credential expired. Rotate the credential in the secret store, rerun the job manually and confirm the vault shows a new recovery point.

title: Backup retention policy
text: Daily backups are kept seven days, weekly backups five weeks and monthly backups twelve months. A legal hold overrides deletion.

title: Restore testing schedule
text: Each quarter one production database is restored to the test environment and checked against a known query set. Record how long the restore took, because that duration is the real recovery time objective.

title: VPN client error VPN-809
text: Error VPN-809 means the client could not reach the gateway on UDP 500 and 4500, usually because a hotel or home router blocks them. Switch the client to the TCP 443 profile and connect again.

title: Split tunnel configuration
text: Only internal address ranges route through the tunnel and internet traffic goes direct. If internal sites fail while the VPN shows connected, the client route table is missing the 10.40.0.0/16 route. Reinstall the VPN profile.

title: VPN gateway certificate
text: The VPN gateway presents a certificate issued by the internal CA. Clients fail with error VPN-13801 when that certificate has expired or the root certificate is missing from the device store.

title: Remote working policy
text: Staff working remotely connect through the VPN to reach internal systems. Personal devices may not use the VPN.

title: Renewing the public web certificate
text: The public web certificate renews thirty days before expiry through the ACME job. If the job fails, check that the DNS validation record _acme-challenge was created, then rerun the job.

title: Before a certificate change: notify and stage
text: Before replacing any certificate on a gateway, open a change record, notify the application owners and stage the new certificate on the standby node first.

title: After a certificate change: verify the chain
text: After installing a certificate, verify the full chain with openssl s_client, confirm the expiry date and update the certificate inventory. Monitoring alert CERT-EXP-30 clears within an hour.

title: Internal certificate authority
text: The internal CA issues certificates for internal services. Requests go through the PKI queue, and the CA root is distributed to managed devices by policy.

title: Outbound mail stuck in the relay queue
text: When messages sit in the relay queue, check the smart host connection and the relay disk space. Error MAIL-451 means the downstream server deferred the message, and the relay retries for 48 hours.

title: Shared mailbox access
text: Access to a shared mailbox is granted by adding the user to its mail-enabled group. Changes take up to an hour to appear in the mail client.

title: Phishing report handling
text: Messages reported with the phishing button go to the SEC-TRIAGE queue. Analysts purge confirmed phishing from all mailboxes and block the sender domain.

title: Email retention
text: Mail is retained for seven years. Deleted items are recoverable by the user for thirty days.

title: Pod in CrashLoopBackOff
text: A pod in CrashLoopBackOff is restarting because its container exits. Read the previous container logs with kubectl logs --previous and check the exit code.

title: Readiness probe failures during rollout
text: Intermittent 502 errors from the ingress during a rolling update are usually readiness probe failures. Increase initialDelaySeconds or fix the health endpoint so pods receive traffic only when ready.

title: Memory limits and OOMKilled
text: A container that exceeds its memory limit is OOMKilled with exit code 137. Raise the limit only after profiling, and set requests equal to limits for critical services.

title: Cluster upgrade calendar
text: Clusters are upgraded one minor version per quarter. Workload owners are notified two weeks before each upgrade.

title: Internal names do not resolve
text: If internal names fail to resolve while public names work, the client is using a public resolver. Check that DHCP handed out 10.40.0.53 and 10.40.0.54, then flush the resolver cache.

title: Adding an internal DNS record
text: Internal A and CNAME records are requested through the DNS form and replicate within fifteen minutes. Records for production require a change record.

title: Split-horizon zones
text: The corp zone is served differently inside and outside the network. External clients receive only public records.

title: Resolver outage DNS-OUT-2
text: Alert DNS-OUT-2 fires when both internal resolvers fail health checks. Fail over to the secondary site resolvers and page the network on-call.

title: Requesting access to an application
text: Application access is requested in the access portal and approved by the application owner. Approved access is granted through group membership within an hour.

title: Quarterly access review
text: Owners review group membership every quarter and remove users who no longer need access. Groups left unreviewed are frozen after thirty days.

title: Leaver process
text: When someone leaves, HR triggers the account disable on their last day. Their mailbox and files are retained for ninety days, then deleted.

title: Privileged access elevation
text: Administrators elevate to privileged roles just in time, for up to eight hours, with a ticket reference. Standing admin rights are not permitted.

title: Update install error UPD-5005
text: Error UPD-5005 means the update agent lacked access to its cache folder. Reset the cache permissions with the repair task and retry the install.

title: Monthly patch window
text: Servers are patched in the monthly window on the second weekend. A critical fix can be expedited through an emergency change.

title: Rolling back a bad update
text: If an update breaks a service, uninstall it from the affected hosts, pause the deployment ring and file a problem record.

title: Patch compliance report
text: The compliance report lists hosts missing updates older than thirty days. Owners of noncompliant hosts are notified weekly.

title: Silencing a noisy alert
text: Create a silence with an expiry and a ticket reference, and never delete the alert rule. A silence longer than seven days needs the service owner's approval.

title: Alert HL-CPU-90 on build agents
text: HL-CPU-90 fires when a build agent exceeds ninety percent CPU for ten minutes. During nightly builds this is expected, so the rule excludes the build window.

title: On-call escalation
text: A page that is not acknowledged within fifteen minutes escalates to the secondary on-call, then to the team lead after thirty minutes.

title: Writing an alert rule
text: Every alert must link a runbook and state the action the responder takes. An alert with no action becomes a dashboard panel instead.

title: Laptop recovery key prompt
text: If a laptop asks for its disk recovery key after a firmware update, the service desk reads the key from the device record after verifying the user. The key rotates after use.

title: Encrypting a new laptop
text: New laptops encrypt the disk automatically at enrolment, and encryption status appears in the device record within a day.

title: Lost or stolen laptop
text: Report a lost laptop to the service desk immediately. The device is wiped remotely and its recovery key is revoked.

title: Device compliance policy
text: Managed devices must be encrypted, patched within thirty days and running the endpoint agent.
